html:
On the night of May 16 to 17, 2010, weather conditions favorable for photography came together.

Here are two images of globular clusters visible in spring in the constellation Hercules.

Messier 92

Located at a distance of 26,000 light-years, this cluster is easily visible with a pair of binoculars.




and Messier 13


Located at a distance of 25,100 light-years, this cluster, 145 light-years in diameter, contains several hundred thousand stars. This cluster is easily visible with a pair of binoculars.




For both photos, here are the technical parameters
Date:  2009/05/16
Optical train = Takahashi Sky90 + f4.5 reducer - IDAS-LPS filter - Canon 40 unfiltered
Mount: Takahashi EM-200 Temma II driven with the SkyVoyager software via Skyfi
Site: At home
10 exposures of 5 min for 50 minutes
Dark, flat and bias applied
DeepSkyStacker + PhotoShop + carboni + neatImage + gradiant Xterminator
Guided with Kwik Guider and the Phd software
